content: If you suspect poisoning, contact a poison control center immediately. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While using this medication, it is essential to undergo laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests or potassium blood level measurements, as directed by your healthcare provider. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to adjust the dosage on your own. For proper storage of this medication, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Discard this product appropriately when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Please note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health needs. Caspofungin is a medication used to treat various fungal infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as echinocandins. This medication is administered via injection into a vein, typically once daily over the course of one hour, as directed by your doctor. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also determined based on body size. If you are using this medication at home, ensure that you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on how to prepare and administer it. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If you notice any abnormalities, do not use the medication and consult your healthcare provider. Infusion reactions may occur during the administration of this drug. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may result in a return of the infection. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or irritation at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any severe symptoms, seek medical attention immediately. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar concerns. Before using caspofungin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other echinocandin antifungal drugs (such as anidulafungin or micafungin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can reach a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests or potassium blood level measurements, should be conducted as directed by your healthcare provider. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to adjust the dosage on your own. For proper storage of this medication, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Discard this product appropriately when it is expired or no longer needed.
